indicators.note: we hear says the word for fortune is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: fortune means fate, one's lot in life

explanation.surface: A carnival earns a lot of money, or so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor festive gathering with stalls and games, a kind of small carnival.

parts.note: flex is the British word for an electric cable, also called a cord

indicators.note: new tells us the following word is to be made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to show off a novel material by bending it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flex' is British English for an electrical lead, not a verb about bending; 'new' signals that the word 'your' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Corduroy is a ridged cotton cloth, so it is a type of fabric.

clue.text: Groups agree to differ about first name

indicators.note: about places the arranged letters around the single letter, so they enclose it
to differ asks the letters of the preceding word to come out different from their order
first takes just the opening letter of the word name

explanation.surface: Two parties agree to differ over what to call something first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to differ' rearranges AGREE into GEERA-type letters, and 'about' wraps them round N, the first letter of 'name'.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a classifying group of species; the plural form names several such groups.

parts.note: leading means top, as in top of the table
a heavy is slang for a villain, especially in a film or play

explanation.surface: The chief bad guy turns out to be mentally unstable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heavier above than below is liable to topple, so it is unbalanced.

indicators.note: taps come marked C and H, cold and hot, so changing taps swaps one of those letters for the other

parts.note: to scrimp is to save money by being thrifty

explanation.surface: A plumber is told to swap the taps in order to economise on the seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath taps are labelled C (cold) and H (hot); 'Change taps' swaps the C in SCRIMP for an H.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimp is a small edible crustacean, a common shellfish.

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped from what precedes
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a sentry is a guard on watch
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Haul a sentry out of bed though he is not dressed in his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GUARD into DRAUG; 'without' then removes U, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag something is to pull it along with effort, so the words are synonyms.

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre or shift about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A racing report: the horse Seed Pod lost its jockey during the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The across clues read as a race card: the capitalised words are horse names and the bracketed words their results. Here 'jockey' shuffles SEEDPOD and 'unseated' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler who is deposed is removed from the throne, unseated from power.

indicators.note: Back means the next word is read in reverse, the way a horse might be backed

parts.note: present means here, as when answering a register

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse called Won Back Present finished out of the places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses WON to make NOW, followed by HERE for 'Present'.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is unplaced finishes outside the top places, so it came in nowhere.

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word Cover

parts.note: finish means end

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse Break Cover came home last.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to tear apart, so it is a synonym of break.

indicators.note: collapsed suggests a structure falling into pieces, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse Large Thin Human collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthling is a person from Earth, a term used in science fiction for a human.

clue.text: Never once arranged to meet again

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, signalling the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A gathering that was never arranged to reconvene.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to assemble once more after a break, meeting again.

indicators.note: evens points to the even-numbered letters, the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of the word

explanation.surface: Race result: the evens favourite was a horse called A Main Vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, evens means odds of one to one; here 'evens' picks letters 2, 4, 6 and 8 of 'favourite'.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the chief artery leaving the heart, the body's main blood vessel.

indicators.note: embraced by means held within, so the name sits inside the longer word

explanation.surface: A woman is warmly hugged by a charity worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is a woman's first name, so it fits the vague definition.

definitions.meaning: to back someone is to support or advocate their cause
the one who comes first in a contest

explanation.surface: Racing advice: put your money on the horse that wins.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion is to support a cause, and a champion is a winner of a contest.

clue.text: Stylish and charming society girl ejected when broadcasting

indicators.note: ejected means thrown out, so one piece is removed from the longer word

parts.note: debonair means suave, stylish and charming
a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society

explanation.surface: A suave debutante gets thrown out of a live show.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is on air while it is being transmitted, so the phrase means when broadcasting.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
I is the Roman numeral for 1

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is taken out

parts.note: a try is a chance or attempt, as in have a try

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse Heartless Metropolis went off at a hundred to one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle R from TRY to leave TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a large and important urban centre, a big city.

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
the figure 1 written as a word
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse Yankee Dollar went off at a thousand to one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollar is a unit of currency, so it is an example of cash, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Distance travelled around university with first piece of chewing gum

indicators.note: around tells us the distance word goes round the other letters

parts.note: milage, a variant spelling of mileage, is distance travelled in miles

indicators.note: first piece of picks the opening letter of the word chewing

explanation.surface: A long trip round a campus with a stick of chewing gum.
explanation.walkthrough: MILAGE is an accepted variant of MILEAGE; 'around' puts U and C after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucilage is a sticky plant secretion or adhesive, a kind of gum.

parts.note: to lay is to place or put down

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse Exterminate came second.
explanation.definitionFit: To slay is to kill, so it is a synonym of exterminate.

clue.text: Fellow sailor provided the maps I fold

indicators.note: fold suggests creasing and refolding a map, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crewmate is handed charts by the narrator to fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate is someone who serves on the same ship, a fellow sailor.

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word place

parts.note: a piece of writing is an article

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse Piece by Piece came first.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny piece or fragment of something.

indicators.note: in a down clue hung up means raised, so the letters read upwards in reverse

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne or sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A fish is hung up to dry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hung up' reverses TO and BRUT together, giving TURB plus OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbot is a large flatfish prized for eating, so it is a fish.

indicators.note: outsider is split into outside plus a letter, so the rank word goes outside that letter

parts.note: a rank is a tier or row

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse The Undertaker was a rank outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: A daring split: 'outsider' is read as 'outside R', putting TIER round R. An undertaker here is one who undertakes, someone who tries.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who undertakes a task is someone who has a go at it, a person who tries.

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician allows the patients to brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous scuffle or struggle, a minor fight.

indicators.note: rolls over suggests tumbling, so the letters are turned into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse Walker's Rest rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the horse name read as plural walkers; the apostrophe is surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Strollers are people who walk at a leisurely pace, so they are walkers.

indicators.note: aboard means on a ship, so one piece is put inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors drink up on board the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to drink in small mouthfuls, so sups means drinks.

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse Turning Space fell.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell is a stretch of high moorland in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A fell is an upland stretch of open hill country, which is moorland.

indicators.note: topping means beheading, so the first letter is picked off the word for cake

parts.note: to cake is to cover thickly, as in boots caked in mud

explanation.surface: A dessert is finished off by pulling the icing off a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cake' is a verb here: caked in mud means covered in mud. Removing the top letter C leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is over it has ended, so the word means finished.

indicators.note: on means the first piece comes in front of, placed on top of, the second

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds at which a horse starts a race
to room is to lodge, to stay as a lodger

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse Room for Mark started as the odds-on favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is horse racing's starting price, the official odds when the race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A splodge is a large irregular blot or mark.

parts.note: even means flat and level
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Race result: the horse Even Number fell.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree or person is to knock them down, laying them out flat.
